hook: Feeding yeast ATP through an imported transporter extended their replicative lifespan
summary: Yeast cells were given a parasite ATP transporter, letting the authors set internal ATP independently of the cell's own supply. Low ATP shortened lifespan and added ATP extended it, and plain extracellular ATP also helped normal cells. The findings are in budding yeast, so whether ATP regulates aging in animals is untested.
title: Engineering ATP import in yeast uncovers a synthetic route to extend cellular lifespan.
